chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Don Redman's physique, sports, pool and ice cream
summary: Redman was about five feet tall and powerfully built, left-handed, played every instrument, played shortstop, shot pool and ate ice cream with Jackson.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Since we're into that, I'd like for you to just describe for our listeners the physique of Don Redmon. He was a very short man.
He was a very short man but he was
built like iron. He was wide. And Don, I'd judge, was about five foot tall. No taller.
No taller.
No taller than five foot tall and he was lefthanded. He conducted lefthanded.
Lefthanded.

He could play every instrument in the band. And he loved sports. I think he said in his younger days he played baseball down there -- his home was in Piedmont, West Virginia -- and he played baseball down there in Virginia with Lefty Grove --
Oh, wow.
-- when they was kids.
Wow. That's interesting.
Yes. And he played shortstop.
Yeah, I could see he was right off the ground, so he --
Oh, sure.
-- he'd get them up.
So he liked sports, a wonderful pool player. I've seen him run 75 balls without stopping.
Wow.
He tried to teach me but I'm not a pool player.
A tremendous ice cream eater.

Oh, we used to eat a pint. Both of us used to go in and get a pint and we'd go to his house, turn the flaps of the buckets open to set it down, and a bowl -- he'd get a bowl for me and a bowl for him -- and we'd sit there and talk until we figure it was melted enough, then we'd just slide the buckets off, you see.
Yeah.
Then you could take your spoon and go all around the sides, you see, where it was soft. But Don Redmon was like a teacher, you see, going back to him, or should we continue the Savoy?
We have enough. The Savoy's great.
(Unintelligible.)
Well, I haven't finished there yet.
